My understanding (based on a conversation with a grammarian coworker a few weeks ago) is that in American English (apparently it's possible British English rules might be different), the period always goes inside the quote marks. The question mark goes inside if you're quoting a question, but on the outside if you're asking a question that includes a quote. Hence:

Dave said "this is the end of the world."

Dave asked "is this the end of the world?"

Did Dave say "this is the end of the world"?

This fits my view of it. However, if I am quoting part of a sentence and I want to end mine, I feel like there are no problems putting the period after the closing quotation mark. Like, following your example:

Dave said "this is the end". (his original sentence was "this is the end of the world." but I only wanted to quote the first four words)

But I could be incorrect.

Logically I agree with you, but according to my coworker the period always goes inside the closing quotation mark, regardless of intention. Hmm, I have another grammar nazi friend (a technical writer and copy editor) who I should ask about this...
